title: Programme Office Ruling on the Premium for a Large Principal Stone
content:
Ruling of the programme office on the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes: a piece whose principal stone is large carries an addition to its valuation, and the addition depends on the value the Belrose Appraisal and Gemological Services report declares for the piece.

## The ruling

Where the principal stone weighs at least one and a half carats (1.5 carats) and the report the register carries for the piece declares it at twenty thousand (20000 USD) or more, eight percent (8 percent) is added. Where the principal stone weighs at least one and a half carats and that report declares it at less than twenty thousand, three percent (3 percent) is added. Where the principal stone weighs less than one and a half carats, nothing is added for the stone's weight.

The weight of the principal stone is the weight recorded on the registration. The value declared is the declared value on the register's issued report for the piece.

## Both sides of each threshold

| Weight of the principal stone | Value the report declares | Added |
|---|---|---|
| 1.5 carats or more | 20000 USD or more | 8 percent |
| 1.5 carats or more | below 20000 USD | 3 percent |
| below 1.5 carats | any | nothing |

A stone of exactly 1.5 carats is at least one and a half carats; one of 1.49 carats is not. A report declaring exactly 20000 USD is at twenty thousand or more; one declaring 19999.99 USD is not.

## Readings on a figure of 12000 USD

- A 2.0-carat stone with a report declaring 25000 USD: 8 percent is added, giving 12960.00 USD.
- A 2.0-carat stone with a report declaring 18000 USD: 3 percent is added, giving 12360.00 USD.
- A 1.0-carat stone, whatever the report declares: 12000.00 USD stands.
